message:
Lena, sunlight covers the daily cold load with cloudy margin using the fixed-tilt monocrystalline array, where Photovoltaic (PV) means solar panels and kilowatt peak (kWp) means rated solar power. Plain words, a parking-space array makes more than twice the daily cooling electricity. Numbers are 8.10 kWh per day from the daily PV yield from 2.4 kWp (E54) against 3.60 kWh per day from the daily electric kWh from 150 W continuous (E52) and 3.61 kWh per day from the steady cooling load and pull-down for 1 tonne box (E24), sane against one-third of a household day.

Farah, Kofi, the night rides through on stored charge using the battery plus controller cabinet, where Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) means the battery chemistry. Plain words, one night uses less than half the stored energy, leaving reserve for cloud. Numbers are 5.12 kWh stored from the EG4 LifePower4 battery datasheet (E9) against about 2.10 kWh for 14 h night at 150 W from the steady electric watts from COP 2.5 (E51), managed by the 60 A controller from the Rover Lite charge controller datasheet (E10), sane against half a household day.

Not ready, because the daily warm-batch limit with Lena and Farah must be locked before wire and fuse sizes freeze.
